_strings.@@5ab6f3719f36: Wisconsin Homestead Credit (property-tax / rent circuit-breaker) — Per the 2024 Form 1 instructions Special Instructions: at least 18 years old on December 31, 2024; if under age 62 and not disabled, must have earned income; a legal resident of Wisconsin for all of 2024; not claimed as a dependent on anyone's 2024 federal return (unless 62 or older); not living in tax-exempt public housing for all of 2024 (exceptions apply); not living in a nursing home receiving Title XIX medical assistance; and not claiming (self or spouse) the veterans and surviving spouses property tax credit or farmland preservation credit. Claimed on Schedule H (or simpler Schedule H-EZ).
_strings.@@6fdd99357875: Treaty conformity — WI conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from WI income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the WI return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Wisconsin Form 1 starts from federal adjusted gross income (2024 Form 1, Line 1; the instructions: fill in federal AGI from line 11 of federal Form 1040 or 1040-SR). Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal AGI and is never added back on the Wisconsin return. The 2024 Schedule AD (Additions to Income) instructions enumerate all addition modifications (Line 1 state and municipal interest; 2 capital gain/loss addition; 3-4 nonqualified Edvest/Tomorrow's Scholar and ABLE distributions; 5 federal NOL deduction; 6 lump-sum distributions (federal Form 4972); 7 PFIC excess distributions; 8 related-entity expenses; 9 expenses for moving a business outside Wisconsin/the U.S.; 10 federal/Wisconsin basis differences; 12 marital-property reporting differences; 13-27 farmland preservation and other computed-credit addbacks; 28-31 tax-option (S) corporation and partnership entity-level adjustments; 32 other) and NONE adds back income exempt under a U.S. tax treaty. Form 1 Line 2 (additions via Schedule I) only converts for federal-law provisions Wisconsin has not adopted, not treaties. Therefore treaty-exempt income flows through and is NOT re-taxed -> conforms = true. (No explicit treaty provision text found at the DOR, so flagged in unverified.)
_strings.@@806f1a35efca: Law change NOT modeled by the engine (status final_form_published): Additional Child and Dependent Care Tax Credit INCREASED and restructured for 2024 — the What's New item reads "The amount of qualifying expenses and maximum credit allowable have been increased", and the credit is now computed on the NEW Schedule WI-2441 (its line 14 carried to Form 1 line 14) instead of being a flat 50% of the federal Form 2441 credit as in 2023. Resolve via: 2024 Schedule WI-2441 and its instructions for the increased qualifying-expense and maximum credit amounts — the schedule was NOT read line-by-line for this pack (see `unverified`); confirm the 2024 dollar caps there before computing the credit.
_strings.@@8e20ba05ad6c: Wisconsin Earned Income Credit (EITC) — Full-year Wisconsin resident who qualifies for the federal earned income credit AND has at least one qualifying child (federal definition of qualifying child applies). A married-filing-separate filer is ineligible unless they meet sec. 7703(b) IRC (then files as head of household, married). "Federal earned income credit" means the credit computed using the IRC as adopted by Wisconsin — filers with Schedule I adjustments recompute it on Schedule I Part III. A copy of federal Schedule EIC must be included (and Form 8867 if a paid preparer was used).

Pack notes: 2024 INDEXATION, NO RATE CHANGE: the four rates 3.5% / 4.4% / 5.3% / 7.65% carry over from 2023 (Act 19 rates; the 2024 What's New lists no rate change), while the dollar boundaries re-indexed — single/HoH $14,320 / $28,640 / $315,310 (2023: $13,810 / $27,630 / $304,170); MFJ $19,090 / $38,190 / $420,420 (2023: $18,420 / $36,840 / $405,550); MFS $9,550 / $19,090 / $210,210 (2023: $9,210 / $18,420 / $202,780). Unlike 2023 there was no mid-year retroactive rate act; the 2024 Form 1-ES schedules and the filing-season Form 1 worksheet agree. Base guidance: Supply 2024 Wisconsin Form 1, Line 11 ('Subtract line 10c from line 9. If line 10c is larger than line 9, fill in 0. This is taxable income'). Line 11 = Wisconsin income (Line 7) minus the sliding-scale standard deduction (Line 8, from the 2024 Standard Deduction Table, p.35) minus Line 10c exemptions ($700 x exemptions on Line 10a + $250 x age-65 checkboxes on Line 10b). Those deductions/exemptions must be computed on the form BEFORE supplying the base — this pack ships no standard deduction and no exemptions, so nothing is re-subtracted here. SOURCE ASSEMBLY: the 2024 Form 1 booklet prints no single four-bracket rate schedule. Brackets 1-2 (rates and dollar boundaries $14,320/$28,640 single-HOH, $19,090/$38,190 MFJ, $9,550/$19,090 MFS) are from the 2024 Form 1-ES '2024 Tax Rate Schedules for Full-Year Residents'; brackets 3-4 (5.3% up to $315,310/$420,420/$210,210, then 7.65%) are from the Form 1 p.44 Tax Computation Worksheet. Cross-check: every worksheet subtraction constant equals the cumulative sum of the prior brackets — Single/HOH $386.64 exact and $7,796.43 vs exact $7,796.425; MFJ $515.52 and $10,395.39 both exact; MFS $257.76 exact and $5,197.70 vs exact $5,197.695 — and every 1-ES gross-tax constant ($501.20/$1,131.28/$16,324.79; $668.15/$1,508.55/$21,766.74; $334.25/$754.01/$10,883.37) equals the cumulative marginal sum exactly. Max divergence $0.005 (cent rounding), immaterial. TABLE MANDATE below $100,000 — Form 1 Line 12 requires the Tax Table (instructions pp.38-43) when Line 11 is under $100,000; the table computes tax at the midpoint of each income band, so bracket math may differ by a few dollars within table bands; the filed form must use the table. At $100,000 or more the mandated Tax Computation Worksheet IS exact bracket math (identical to this pack). STANDARD DEDUCTION NOT SHIPPED (income-dependent): Wisconsin's standard deduction is a sliding amount from the 2024 Standard Deduction Table (p.35) based on Line 7 income — maximums $13,230 single / $24,490 married filing jointly / $11,630 married filing separately / $17,090 head of household, phasing to $0 as income rises. Filers claimable as a dependent use the Standard Deduction Worksheet for Dependents (greater of $1,300 or earned income + $450, capped at the table amount); short-period filers and federal Form 4563 filers get $0. Compute it on Form 1 Line 8 — the supplied Line 11 base is already net of it. EXEMPTIONS NOT SHIPPED (already inside the Line 11 base): Wisconsin's exemptions ARE base reductions — $700 per exemption on Line 10a (taxpayer, spouse, and each dependent listed on federal Form 1040; $0 for a filer claimable as a dependent on another return) plus $250 on Line 10b for taxpayer and/or spouse 65 or older on December 31, 2024 (only if allowed the $700 on Line 10a) — but they are subtracted on the form in arriving at Line 11, so this pack ships none; do NOT re-subtract them from the supplied base. Head of household uses the SAME rate schedule as single (Tax Computation Worksheet Section A 'Single or Head of household'; 2024 Form 1-ES Schedule A 'Single, Head of Household, Estates and Trusts'). Estates and trusts (fiduciaries) also use this schedule. QUALIFYING SURVIVING SPOUSE — engine mapping is WRONG for Wisconsin: Wisconsin has no QSS status; per the 2024 Form 1 instructions, 'If you file your federal return as a qualifying surviving spouse, you may file your Wisconsin return as head of household.' A federal QSS (spouse died 2022 or 2023) must therefore use the head_of_household brackets here, NOT married_filing_jointly. (A taxpayer whose spouse died during 2024 may still file 2024 as married filing jointly.) FULL-YEAR RESIDENT Form 1 ONLY: nonresidents and part-year residents file Form 1NPR and must PRORATE the tax brackets by the ratio of Wisconsin income to federal adjusted gross income (2024 Form 1-ES instructions print the proration rule with a worked example) — applying these brackets unprorated to a 1NPR filer is wrong. Credits taken after Line 12 are NOT modeled (they are subtracted from tax, not from income): itemized deduction credit (Line 13, Schedule 1), additional child and dependent care credit (Line 14, NEW Schedule WI-2441 for 2024), blind worker transportation services credit (Line 15, new for 2024, up to $1,500), renter's/homeowner's school property tax credit (Line 16, max $300/$150), married couple credit (Line 18, Schedule 2, max $480), earned income credit (Line 30, 4%/11%/34% of federal EIC), homestead credit (Line 33), and other Form 1 credits.
